scope: Read-only source/history audit of Marathon runtime integration, pinned patch stack and identified local backend source trees. No private conversations, model contents, snapshots or runtime logs read. No builds, GPU work, model tests or runtime replacement.
recommendation: Stage a separate clean v1.0.0 candidate and benchmark before migration. Do not git-pull/rebase the tuned runtime in place or replay all 14 patches blindly.

unpackaged_source_changes.head: ca461b488
unpackaged_source_changes.comparison: Reconstructed 14-patch base differs from this working tree in five touched files. Substantive differences are compact/exact8 Q8 attention in fattn-vec.cuh and optional draft/debug telemetry in server-context.cpp/server-task.cpp/server-task.h. common/speculative.cpp differences are whitespace/cast spelling. This comparison covers patch-touched files, not every possible untracked artifact.
unpackaged_source_changes.action: Preserve the existing tree; explicitly include the extra kernel in future benchmark/port inventory.

integration_findings: scripts/apply_llamacpp_patches.sh rejects a qwen38 base different from config/llamacpp-qwen38.ref. Changing the pin alone then encounters the patch conflicts.

Marathon talks to llama-server over HTTP. Public C API removals primarily affect the fork/build, not a directly linked Python client. Speculation APIs moved/changed, including llama_set_embd_state_src -> llama_set_ctx_state_src.
Sequence-state version changed 3 -> 4; session version 10 -> 11. Treat old binary slot caches as incompatible. Do not attempt to reuse sidecars across the migration.

Upstream persists checkpoints and draft state as appendices in one slot file; Marathon currently also tracks .draft/.spec/.checkpoints sidecars. New caches and save/restore/accounting regression tests are required.
marathon_app/runtime.py _backend_cache_id includes command, environment and binary path/size/mtime. This should separate a new binary from prior caches; validate rather than bypass the guard.

Catalog Qwen long-option names were found in upstream common/arg.cpp, including reasoning-preserve, backend-sampling, checkpoint-min-step and load-mode. This static name check does not validate argument values or endpoint behavior.
The generic run_llama_server.sh fallback still prefers historical third_party/.marathon paths; setup/build use ~/AI/backends. Use explicit candidate binary paths during comparisons.

deepseek.findings: Upstream includes DeepSeek4/4.1 and draft-mtp, but not the catalog dsv4-mtp spec type or DSV4_CONSTANT_SHAPE/IDX_SKIP/MOE_TILE/SPARSE_FA/MTP_SPEC hooks. Therefore existing DeepSeek profiles are not drop-in replacements. Exact fork ancestry/merge conflict enumeration and GGUF compatibility were not tested; these need a separate migration track.

relevant_upstream_changes.description: Fused DFlash encoder and KV injection

next_steps: Build a separately named stock v1.0.0 candidate pinned to the exact audited SHA; retain current binaries and source unchanged. Follow manage-local-gpu before any GPU work.

Use synthetic/public prompts only. Compare old tuned binary vs stock v1 with identical model, KV types, GPU placement and sampling: prefill, decode, short/long context, draft acceptance and time per accepted token.
Exercise text, image/media, tool calling, streaming, cancellation, cold/warm prefix reuse, slot save/restore, divergent-prefix recurrent rewind and host/VRAM usage.
Benchmark remaining IQ4_XS crossover, Q8 fused attention, cache preference and unpackaged compact/exact8 kernel individually. Retire overlaps only after measured correctness/performance parity.
Update runtime profile and cache identity with fresh caches only after tests pass. Keep DeepSeek migration separate.
